routine: C0/9C37 z-gate + C0/9C5C per-axis collision-apply + C0/9CA1 trigger-region lookup + C0/9D54 plane update + C0/9D6E conveyor/auto-move + C0/9DC3 scene-load init (the collision-commit cluster). DP=$1D00.
summary: This is the collision-COMMIT half of the field player mover. 9C37 is the z-plane solidity gate (carry SET = solid). 9C5C is the per-axis commit worker: it computes the tentative next position ($66/$70 = $62 + $2E for X, $68 = $64 + $30 for Y, with a +/-$100 row wrap into $72), refetches the destination tile props (9AC8 prop-fetch + 9AD3 shape-decode) and z-gates it (9C37); if solid it zeros the velocity ($2E/$30) and returns (the move is blocked), otherwise it falls through to: (a) the 9CA1 trigger/touch-region lookup ($7E7080 16-bit index plane -> *7 record in the $E50000 ROM table, matching tileX/tileY and a Y-proximity test, writing trigger fields $0112-$0116 and setting $0117 bit7 "trigger armed"); (b) a DOOR/special check on $7E7000 bit4 (sets $0117 bit4, latches the cell into $015B); (c) the 9D54 plane update (player Z $0155 := tile z $6A unless IGNORE_Z $6C set; OBJ priority $0C00/$0C01[$0197] := $6E/$6F); and (d) the 9D6E conveyor: tile byte1 ($5A) bits 0x0C pick a speed (0x20/0x08/0x10) and bits 0x03 pick a direction, writing the per-frame momentum seed $2A/$2B (signed). 9DC3 is the once-per-scene-load init that seeds $0155 and the party OBJ priorities from the spawn tile. NOTE: the actual single caller of 9C5C is C0/8AFE inside the right-move driver at 8AB5 (and its mirror per-direction drivers via 8A6D dispatch); 9C5C itself only runs once all the leading-edge probes (8A9E -> 9AA1/9AD3/9C37) have already passed.
dp: $1D00 (so dp operand $XX = WRAM $7E:1DXX). Exceptions noted inline: 9DC3 re-establishes D=$1D00 itself via PHD/LDA #$1D00/TCD at 9DDE-9DE4, after writing some absolute $7F0Cxx bytes with the prior D.
wramReads: $1D2E ($2E) = X velocity accumulator (16-bit, signed), added to base X for tentative pos
$1D30 ($30) = Y velocity accumulator (16-bit, signed); bit15 (BIT #$0080 on hi byte) selects row-wrap direction
$1D62 ($62) = base position X (16-bit) -- the committed player X this frame
$1D64 ($64) = base position Y (16-bit)
$1D66/$1D67 ($66/$67) = tentative next X (16-bit); $67 hi byte = destination cell X
$1D68/$1D69 ($68/$69) = tentative next Y (16-bit); $69 hi byte = destination cell Y
$1D6A ($6A) = tile z-plane (0..3) output of 9AD3; read by 9C37 gate and 9D54 plane update and 9DF8 spawn
$1D6C ($6C) = IGNORE_Z flag (byte2&4, 8-bit nonzero); gates 9C37 special-case and 9D54 plane update
$1D6E/$1D6F ($6E/$6F) = computed OBJ sprite priority low/high (from byte1/byte2 >>2 &0x10 |0x20)
$1D5A ($5A) = scene tile property byte1; bits 0x0C=conveyor speed sel, 0x03=conveyor dir, used in 9D6E
$1D5C ($5C) = scene tile property byte2 (z-plane source, used by 9AD3)
$1D58 ($58) = scene tile property byte0 (shape source, used by 9AD3)
$1D5E ($5E) = one-way/slope scratch (output of 9AD3 shape 0x1C path); copied to $34 and $1D34
$1D70/$1D71 ($70/$71) = copy of tentative X / its hi cell byte (door secondary probe)
$1D72/$1D73 ($72/$73) = row-wrap neighbour Y ($68 -/+ 0x100) / its hi cell byte (door secondary probe)
$1D1E ($1E) = X cell mask (0x0F/0x1F/0x3F per map width; scene-load 73AA-73B6)
$1D1F ($1F) = Y cell mask (per map height; scene-load 73CF-73E1)
$1D04 ($04) = trigger-table row base offset added to idx*7 (9CCE); UNCERTAIN exact writer
$1D52 ($52) = scratch (trigger flags byte / conveyor speed)
$1D34 ($34) = one-way+conveyor flag scratch (bit3 set when on conveyor)
$0155 = player Z-plane (absolute); read by 9C37 gate, written by 9D54/9DFE
$0197 = player actor index (absolute); indexes $0C00/$0C01
$0199 = party member 2 actor index (9E0E)
$019B = party member 3 actor index (9E17)
$0117 = trigger/door state flags (absolute): bit7=trigger armed, bit4=door pending; read+written 9CA1/9D24/9D4A
$0102 = spawn cell index (16-bit, absolute) read at scene-load 9DE5
$7E70C0,X = off-map/solid sentinel plane (bit7) -- via 9AB2
$7E30C0,X / $7E7000,X / $7E7040,X = tile property byte0/byte1/byte2 planes (via 9AB2)
$7E7000,X (door check) bit4 = DOOR_TRIGGER, tested at 9D43 on the wrap-neighbour cell
$7E7080,X = 16-bit trigger-region INDEX plane; bit15 set = no trigger; else *7 -> $E50000 record (9CB7)
$E50000+rec ROM trigger table, 7 bytes/record: [0]=tileX,[1]=tileY,[3]->$0112,[4]=flags(->$0116 lo nibble, bit7, ->$0113 bit0),[5]->$0114,[6]->$0115
$4216 (RDMPYL) = hardware multiply result idx*7 (9CCA)
wramWrites: $1D2E ($2E) := 0 and $1D30 ($30) := 0 -- BLOCK move when destination z-solid [9C9A/9C9C]
$0116 := ((E50004 flags)>>1)&0x0F, then OR bit7 of flags [9CFE/9D05]
$0155 := $6A (player z-plane := tile z-plane) unless IGNORE_Z [9D5A]; := (spawn z, 0->1) at scene-load [9DFE]
$1D52 ($52) := conveyor speed (0x08/0x10/0x20) [9D7E/9D84/9D8A] or trigger flag byte [9CF9]
$2A/$2B ($1D2A/$1D2B) := conveyor momentum seed: +/-speed on the selected axis, 0 on the other [9D9E/9DA5/9DAF/9DB7]; both 0 when no conveyor [9DBE/9DC0]
uncertainties: $1D04 ($04) trigger-table ROW BASE: I confirmed the lookup forms rec = (idx*7) + $04 into $E50000, but the writer of $1D04 in this DP context is not pinned. The 3B39/3B8F STA $04 sites are a DMA save/restore (different context). Likely $04 is set during scene load alongside the $7E7080 index plane build; verify the writer and whether it is 0 in the single-screen field-walk case.

The $E50000 record layout (7 bytes) is inferred from the field offsets read ([0]=tileX,[1]=tileY,[3..6] payload, [2] unread/unknown). The decoded header bytes [0x02,0x04,0x10,0x04,0x1e,0x04,...] at E50000 look like a u16 pointer/dispatch table per LOCATION rather than the records themselves -- i.e. $7E7080 may already index into a per-location sub-table and $04 selects the location. This whole trigger subsystem is NOT exercised by disasm/boot_trace_play.txt (grep found 0 hits for 9CA1/9CB7/9CD3), so it is UNVALIDATED against a trace. For the M1 player-mover port the trigger path only matters for $0117/$0112-0116 side effects; the position residual (the stated goal) is unaffected by it.

The 9D2C primary-cell index recompute ($69/$67 -> 9D2C..9D33) is immediately overwritten by the wrap-cell index ($73/$71 -> 9D35..9D3C) before TAX, so for the DOOR check the index used is ALWAYS the row-wrap neighbour ($73/$71). The 9D2C..9D33 computation is dead code on the fall-through path (live only as the BRL target's no-op lead-in). Worth a verifier double-check that no path uses the 9D2C value in X.

Conveyor direction mapping: dir bits 00/01/10/11 -> I read them as up(-Y)/down(+Y)/left(-X)/right(+X) from the DEC-A dispatch (9D94 BEQ 9DB4 = case0=-Y; 9D96 DEC BEQ 9DAD = case1=+Y; 9D99 DEC BEQ 9DA3 = case2=-X; fall = case3=+X). The +Y/-Y vs +X/-X axis assignment ($2A=X-momentum, $2B=Y-momentum) follows the KEY WRAM doc ($2A/$2B seed $2E/$2/30 via 88E5) but the exact screen-direction sign convention (is +$2B down or up on screen) should be cross-checked against the velocity-apply side in C0/88E5/9175.

9C5C has exactly ONE static caller: C0/8AFE (in the rightward-move driver 8AB5, reached from the 8A6D direction dispatch when $2E>0,$30==0). The mirror directions (8BC4/8E21/8EF1/8FC1/909C/8D11) presumably each have their own commit; I traced only the right path in full. The $62/$64 base-pos and the +0x70/-0x40 sub-cell offsets at 8AB5 (foot/head probe geometry) belong to the CALLER, not 9C5C -- 9C5C just adds $2E/$30 to whatever $62/$64 hold. Confirm the other 5 direction drivers set $62/$64 the same way before calling 9C5C (or an equivalent).

9C5C runs REP #$20 (16-bit A) for the tentative-pos math but the prop-fetch/gate run SEP #$20 (8-bit); I traced the REP/SEP toggles at 9C5C/9C89/9C98/9CC8/9CD1 and the X-width toggles at 9CB4/9D52/9E26. The verifier should confirm A-width is 8-bit on entry to 9C37 (it is: 9C89 SEP before 9C8D, and 9C8B LDA $67 is 8-bit) since 9C37's compares are byte compares.

9AD3 shape-decode: I summarized its outputs ($6A z, $6C ignoreZ, $6E/$6F prio, $5E one-way) and the slope-table mechanism (C09BF5/9C0B/9C21) but did not fully verify each slope shape's pass/fail math -- it is upstream of my focus cluster (9C37 onward). The byte-exactness of the SOLID decision depends on it; flag for the shape-decode owner.
